BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to funding pollution abatement and response; addingnew sections to chapter 70.94 RCW; adding a new section to chapter90.56 RCW; and providing an expiration date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.94 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In addition to other fees and taxes required under this chapter,registered owners of motor vehicles as defined in RCW 46.04.320 shallannually, upon renewal, pay a clean air fee of two dollars. Eightyseven and onehalf percent of the proceeds from the clean air fee mustbe deposited in a segregated subaccount of the air pollution controlaccount created in RCW 70.94.015, and twelve and onehalf percent ofthe proceeds from the clean air fee must be deposited in the vesselresponse account in section 3 of this act.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.94 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Money from the clean air fee under section 1 of this act that p. 1 SB 6072is deposited in the segregated subaccount of the air pollution controlaccount created in RCW 70.94.015 may be used for the purposes of thischapter, including the following: (a) Retrofitting school buses with exhaust emission controldevices; (b) Reducing vehicle air contaminant emissions and cleaning up airpollution; (c) Reducing and monitoring toxic air contaminants; (d) Providing funding for fueling infrastructure necessary to allowschool bus fleets to use alternative, cleaner fuels. (2) Money from the clean air fee under section 1 of this actdeposited in the segregated subaccount of the air pollution controlaccount created in RCW 70.94.015 is subject to distribution as follows: (a) Eightyfive percent of the money must be distributed to the airpollution control authorities created under this chapter. The moneymust be distributed in direct proportion with the amount of feesimposed under section 1 of this act that are collected within theboundaries of each authority. However, an amount in direct proportionwith those fees collected in counties for which no air pollutioncontrol authority exists must be distributed to the department. (b) Fifteen percent of the money from the fee under section 1 ofthis act must be distributed to the department and used by thedepartment for the following purposes: (i) Retrofitting school buses with exhaust emission controldevices; (ii) Reducing vehicle air contaminant emissions and cleaning up airpollution; (iii) Reducing and monitoring toxic air contaminants; (iv) Providing funding for fueling infrastructure necessary toallow school bus fleets to use alternative, cleaner fuels. (3) Money in the air pollution control account may be spent by thedepartment only after appropriation. (4) The department shall provide a report to the legislativetransportation committees on the progress of the implementation of thissection by December 31, 2004.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.56 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The vessel response account is created in the state treasury.Receipts from the clean air fee in section 1 of this act shall bedeposited into the account. Moneys in the account may be spent onlyafter appropriation. Expenditures from the account may be used by thedepartment of ecology for a dedicated rescue tug, deployed at theentrance of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, whose primary mission is toarrest the drift of disabled vessels to prevent a pollution event. Thetug may also be equipped and available to provide other emergencyservices and assistance including intervention support for thecoordinated vessel traffic service, assisting search and rescueefforts, marine fire fighting, and early oil spill response.
Section 1 of this act expires July 1, 2008.
